fields.features_heading: What a Peel Consent Record Holds
fields.features_subheading: What a chemical peel consent form should carry before a provider applies an acid, and what the front desk needs later.
fields.feature_1:
The peel named before anything else

Choose the agent and depth before the client signs. A superficial glycolic peel and a medium-depth TCA peel show different risk statements, and the form picks the right set.
fields.feature_2:
Screening that reaches the provider

Ask about isotretinoin and a history of cold sores in your provider's own words. Any answer that needs a second look reaches the provider while there is still time to call.
fields.feature_3:
Fitzpatrick type on the record

Record the client's Fitzpatrick skin type at consultation. Pick which types need a test spot, and the full consent stays closed until a provider has checked that spot.
fields.feature_4:
A signature for every session

Mild peels are often booked as a series. Each session opens with the client's previous answers filled in, and the strength used is saved next to that day's signature.
fields.feature_5:
Aftercare the client initials

Turn each aftercare instruction your provider gives into a line to initial. A check-in form follows a few days later and sends any reply about blistering to the nurse.
fields.feature_6:
Source code your clinic keeps

Export the full code to your GitHub repository. A developer can place the peel consent inside your booking site, add a field for a new peel and keep changing it there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Ways Clinics Run Peel Consent
fields.tab_content_1:
Before Tess calls, an isotretinoin yes holds the booking

Wren Day Spa sends the consent 48 hours before every peel. Clients answer esthetician Tess Morgan's screening questions, including whether they take or have ever taken isotretinoin or get cold sores. A yes on either holds the booking and puts the form in Tess's queue. She calls the client before the visit.
fields.tab_content_2:
For type IV skin, a test spot comes first

Dr. Elena Park performs medium-depth peels at Larkspur Dermatology. Her consent records the peel agent and depth beside the client's Fitzpatrick type. For type IV and darker skin, the practice books a test spot first. The full peel consent opens only after she checks the spot seven days later and marks it clear.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each peel in the series has its own signature and strength

Nora Diaz is booked for five glycolic peels at Maple Row Med Spa. Before peel three, her form opens with her last answers filled in. She confirms her medications and signs again. Her record lists each peel with the strength used and its signature.
fields.tab_content_4:
On day three, the check-in asks about blistering

Before a client leaves Sable Skin Studio, she initials each aftercare line her provider went over. On day three, a short check-in form asks how her skin looks. Hannah Cole reports a small blister, and the form sends her answer to Jo Reyes, the nurse on duty, who calls her that afternoon.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Chemical Peel Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work is deciding what your provider explains before a peel and what each client must answer first.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name each peel on your menu
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about isotretinoin and cold sores
fields.howto_step_1_des: Note what your provider tells every client before a peel: what the acid does, the side effects they mention and the other options, including no peel at all. The consent form records that conversation, and its wording should match what clients hear in the room.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List your peels by agent and depth, for example a superficial glycolic peel or a medium-depth trichloroacetic acid peel. Each one gets its own risk statements, and a client sees only the statements for the peel she booked.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The American Academy of Dermatology asks patients to tell their dermatologist about isotretinoin, past or current, and about cold sores. Write those questions in your provider's words and decide which answers hold a booking for review.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add the Fitzpatrick scale, which sorts skin into six types by how it burns and tans. If your practice runs a test spot for some types, set that rule here and keep the full consent closed until someone checks the spot.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your peel menu and screening questions. Emergent builds the consent form and its review queue, with a table that holds one row per signed peel. Ask for changes in plain English, such as a Spanish version or a photo upload.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Attach the consent link to every appointment confirmation and email the client a PDF of what she signed. Emergent connects to any tool with an API, including the booking software or practice management system your front desk already uses.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it, then have it reviewed
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign the form twice yourself, once with a yes on isotretinoin and once without, then open both records. Ask your medical director and a healthcare attorney to read the wording before the first client signs it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is spa and clinic PDFs, a day spa's online form and one Jotform template, and each is a single sheet signed once whatever the peel. A peel consent changes with the agent, the depth and the client's skin, and mild peels are usually booked as a series, so this page shows the consent working where those differences matter: a day spa that pauses a booking when a client reports isotretinoin, a dermatology practice that records the agent, depth and Fitzpatrick type and runs a test spot first for darker skin, a med spa logging each peel of a five-session series with its own signature, and a studio whose aftercare acknowledgment leads to a day-three check-in.
tab_stories: Wren Day Spa sends the consent 48 hours before a peel, and a yes on the isotretinoin or cold sore question pauses the booking and puts the form in esthetician Tess Morgan's queue so she can call before the visit.

At Larkspur Dermatology, Dr. Elena Park records the peel agent, the depth and the client's Fitzpatrick type on the consent, and a client with type IV or darker skin gets a test spot, with the full peel consent opening only after the spot is checked a week later.
Nora Diaz is on peel three of a five-peel glycolic series at Maple Row Med Spa, re-confirms her screening answers and signs again, and her record lists each peel with its strength and her signature.
Before leaving Sable Skin Studio, a client initials each aftercare line, and on day three a check-in form asks how her skin looks, sending any report of blistering to the nurse on duty.

claims_to_source: Informed consent documentation covers the nature of the procedure, its risks and benefits, reasonable alternatives and the patient's understanding

Mild peels often need 3 to 5 treatments spaced 2 to 4 weeks apart

Without the right expertise, people with skin of color can develop permanent pigment problems after a chemical peel
The Fitzpatrick scale sorts skin into six types by how it burns and tans
